title: Log and Control Forwarding: how a Connector's logs and control traffic reach the Zscaler cloud
aliases: cloud connector logs not reaching zscaler

prose.label: Where it sends.
prose.text: This policy carries only the first leg of a log's path to a SIEM; NSS carries the second: [[cloud-connector.nss-va.log-control-path:two-legs]].

prose.label: Rule fields.
prose.text: {{rule-order}} Whether evaluation stops at the first match is open: [[cloud-connector.nss-va.log-control-path:rule-first-match]]. {{rule-fields}} Whether the API enforces the console's name and description limits is open {{gap:limit-enforcement}}.

prose.label: In the API.
prose.text: {{tf-forward-method}} {{gateway-type}} {{dns-gateway-no-type}} The Go SDK's dns_forwarding_gateway package nevertheless gives /dnsGateways a `type` whose comment names ECSELF: [[cloud-connector.terraform.gateways:structs-differ]]; whether the API uses it is open: [[cloud-connector.terraform.gateways:dns-gateway-type-semantics]].

What happens to logs when the gateway is unreachable: [[cloud-connector.nss-va.log-control-path:log-upload-starvation]]. Effects on enrollment and policy delivery, and on Connectors no rule covers, are not stated {{gap:channel-failure}}. Names of predefined log rules are not captured: [[cloud-connector.terraform.rule-protection:predefined-log-rule-names]].

checks.do: Which Log and Control rule covers the Connector's location or group, and which Log and Control gateway it uses.
For logs expected in a SIEM, the NSS configuration rather than this policy.

default-rule.statement: A default Log and Control Forwarding rule with a default gateway action is created automatically, and it cannot be duplicated or deleted.

quotes: A default log and control forwarding rule with a default gateway forwarding action is automatically created.
You cannot duplicate or delete the default log and control forwarding rule.

gateways.statement: The policy configures the primary and secondary gateways used to set up control channels and forward logs.

quotes: Log and control forwarding provides the following benefits and enables you to:
Configure the primary and secondary gateways used for setting up control channels and forwarding logs.

rule-order.statement: Log and Control rules are evaluated in ascending numerical order; a disabled rule is skipped but keeps its place.

quotes: Forwarding rules are evaluated in ascending numerical order (Rule 1 before Rule 2), and the Rule Order reflects this rule's place in the order.
When you select Disabled, the service skips it and moves to the next rule. However, the rule does not lose its place in the Rule Order.

rule-fields.statement: A rule's name is at most 31 characters; its source is all locations or up to 8, or all or specific Cloud & Branch Connector groups; its action is a Log and Control Gateway; its description is at most 10,240 characters.

quotes: Location/Sublocation: Click Select All to apply the rule to all locations, or select up to 8 locations.
Cloud & Branch Connector Groups: Click Select All to apply the rule to all groups, or select specific groups to apply the rule.
From the Gateway drop-down menu, choose an appropriate Log and Control Gateway

tf-forward-method.statement: In Terraform, a log forwarding rule's `forward_method` has the single supported value `ECSELF`, and the rule names its gateway in `proxy_gateway`.

quotes: * `forward_method` - (String) The type of traffic forwarding method selected from the available options. Supported value: `ECSELF`
* `proxy_gateway` - (List of Object) The proxy gateway for which the rule is applicable.

gateway-type.statement: The Log and Control gateway is a forwarding gateway on the API's `/gateways` endpoint: its `type` enum is PROXYCHAIN, ZIA and ECSELF, with ECSELF described as the Log and Control gateway.

expect.description: Type of the gateway. Supported types are ZIA and ECSELF (Log and Control gateway).

dns-gateway-no-type.statement: The contract's DNS gateway object (`/dnsGateways`) has no `type` member; it carries `dnsGatewayType` instead, with the values OFW_PDNS_REDIR_GW and EC_DNS_GW.

limit-enforcement.title: Whether the API enforces the console's rule name and description limits
limit-enforcement.detail: The console limits a Log and Control rule's name to 31 characters and its description to 10,240; the Go SDK models both as plain strings. Whether the API rejects longer values, and whether DNS rule fields carry similar limits, is unconfirmed.
limit-enforcement.blocks: predicting API errors for long names or descriptions

channel-failure.title: Effects of a Log and Control path failure on enrollment and policy, and of a Connector no rule covers
channel-failure.detail: Unverified legacy statements: DNS Policy outcomes are logged through Log and Control Forwarding, so a block with no cloud event usually means this channel is broken; an outage causes stale policy delivery, and enrollment and policy sync can fail silently while the Connector appears registered; Connectors not covered by a narrow rule use the default rule, and a wrong default gateway silently degrades log delivery. None is stated by a captured source. Log loss itself is in cloud-connector.nss-va.log-control-path:log-upload-starvation.
channel-failure.blocks: diagnosing missing logs or stale policy on a Connector
